inputs.share_count_basis: 48.768m shares issued and outstanding at 2026-10-27 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover, after the Q3 repurchase) plus ~0.13m treasury-method dilution (Q3-2026 diluted less basic weighted average). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; 1.577m unvested RSU/PSU/MPSU units are the forward SBC charge, not an extra dilution layer.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement add-back, TTM to 2026-09-30 (FY2025 10-K 227.4 less 9M-2025 173.6 plus 9M-2026 200.3). No net-share-settlement tax line exists in financing activities (awards use sell-to-cover), so there is no equity-award tax to add. FY2026E SBC is ~323 (9M 200.3 + Q4 guidance 121-125), 7.4% of FY2026E revenue; the H2-2026 run-rate is ~9% after the 2026 MPSU grants.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Cost of equity = US 10-year risk-free ~4.25% + beta ~1.25 x ERP ~4.75% = ~10.2%; no debt, so WACC = cost of equity, rounded to 10.0%. One WACC in all three scenarios: customer-concentration and AI-cycle risk is charged through the scenario paths and the 25% bear weight, not through a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ignored as immaterial: total lease liabilities were 24.1 at FY2025 against ~4,300 of revenue. Lease cost stays inside operating expenses (EBITDA is after it) and no lease liability is in net debt.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (dcf-methods routing row 1: US fabless operating company; no adaptations file needed). First valuation of this ticker. FY0 = FY2026E: 9M-2026 actual revenue 2,987.2 plus the Q4 guidance midpoint 1,350 = 4,337 (+55.4% on FY2025); year 1 is FY2027. last_fcf / reported_fcf / sbc / interest_income are TTM actuals to 2026-09-30 (OCF 873.0 less capex 263.6 = 609.4 reported; less SBC 254.1 and interest income 32.4 = 322.9 owner FCF). TTM owner FCF is depressed by a working-capital build (receivables +206, inventories +200 in 9M-2026) and capacity capex at ~7% of revenue; the forward build carries both explicitly rather than extrapolating the TTM margin. NET CASH: cash 560.5 + short-term investments 530.7 = 1,091.2, no borrowings (2026-09-30). Net cash is >1x the owner-FCF base so interest income is stripped. One quarter of FY2026 cash flow (Q4) falls between the balance sheet and the first modelled year and is not counted - a small conservative gap. NOT IN THE BRIDGE: (1) the 1,183 net deferred tax asset from the foreign tax incentive (restated FY2024) - it has not begun to unwind (9M-2026 deferred taxes -0.3) and its utilisation schedule is not disclosed, so the cash-tax path is set at roughly the GAAP rate with no shelter; if it shelters cash tax later it is upside of at most ~$24/share undiscounted. (2) Any securities-class-action liability (Feb-Nov 2024 class period) - unquantified. BUYBACKS: 457.5 repurchased in 9M-2026 (453.4 in Q3), 535.9 authorisation remaining at 2026-09-30; with SBC running ~320-500/yr the flat-count convention is now broadly funded, where FY2025 (6.6 repurchased) it was not. Dividends are ~$8/share/yr and are a use of FCF, not a deduction. GOVERNANCE FLAGS: unremediated material weakness in deferred-tax controls and FY2024 restatement; tax-related figures carry more than usual uncertainty. CONCENTRATION: Enterprise Data is 42% of Q3-2026 revenue (+165% YoY) and substantially one platform relationship (Nvidia); top-3 distributors 54% of FY2025 revenue. Growth paths deliberately decelerate hard from the FY2026 +55% rather than extrapolate it.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (28-30%) is not usable as the anchor: FY2024 equity was lifted ~1.0bn by a one-time deferred-tax benefit (foreign tax incentive, restated), and it diverges >30% from the 3-year revenue (15.9%) and EPS (12.4%) CAGRs. Revenue 3-year CAGR (FY2022-FY2025, spanning the 2023 downcycle) is used as the through-cycle reference instead.
historical_growth.notes: FY-end basis, FY2025 latest full year. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC less interest income): FY2025 409.5, FY2022 12.5, FY2020 ~117.6 (FY2020 interest income estimated at ~9; not in the KPI table). The 3-year owner-FCF CAGR is not meaningful because FY2022 owner FCF was near zero after an inventory build (reported FCF 187.8 against SBC 161.0). 5-year owner-FCF CAGR 28.3% vs reported 25.7% - SBC has grown slower than cash flow over five years (SBC 10.1% of revenue in FY2020, 8.2% in FY2025), but the 2026 MPSU grants reverse that in H2-2026 (~9%). FY2024 EPS (32.60) is the tax-benefit year and is excluded from any trend reading.

base.rationale: Growth: FY2027 +38% to ~5,985 - the Q4-2026 guided run-rate (1,350/qtr = 5,400 annualised) plus mid-single-digit sequential growth, well short of the ~8bn capacity target for H2-2027; then a hard deceleration to 16% and 11% as the AI power build normalises, fading to 4%. FY2036 revenue ~11.7bn (10-year CAGR ~10% off an elevated base vs 24% for 2015-2025). EBITDA margin is pre-SBC: FY2026E = GAAP operating income ~1,314 + D&A ~70 + SBC ~323 = ~39.4% of revenue; held ~39% (FY2022 40.4%, FY2023 36.9%, FY2025 36.1%) - gross margin has drifted from 58% to 55% as lower-margin AI modules mix in, offsetting opex leverage. SBC 8.5% reflects the H2-2026 MPSU step-up (816 unamortised over ~3 years), gliding to 6.5%. Capex 6% -> 4% (FY2015-25 average ~6%, 9M-2026 7.5% on capacity build); D&A rises toward 3% as that base depreciates. Cash tax 23% -> 22%: 9M-2026 GAAP rate 22.9% (Q3 26.1%), no DTA shelter assumed. Working capital consumes 18% of incremental revenue (9M-2026: net operating working capital absorbed ~190 on a ~950 YoY revenue increase; inventory-heavy model). Terminal: Gordon binds at ~14.7x, below the 18x cap.

bull.rationale: FY2027 +50% to ~6.5bn (sequential growth continues at ~7%/qtr and the ~8bn capacity is being filled by late 2027), FY2028 +28% to ~8.3bn. FY2036 revenue ~17.5bn. Margin expands to 42% pre-SBC on opex leverage with gross margin holding ~55-56%; SBC falls to 5.5% as revenue outgrows the grant base.

bear.rationale: FY2027 +18% to ~5.1bn (below the Q4-2026 run-rate: growth stalls mid-year), then FY2028 -15% as Enterprise Data roughly halves on an AI-capex digestion and/or a lost next-generation socket - the 2024 Enterprise Data episode at four times the scale. Recovery at 3-6%. Pre-SBC margin drops to 33% on deleverage and price concessions and recovers only to 35%; SBC stays 8-10% of a smaller revenue base. The working-capital term releases cash in the down year (inventory liquidation), which is why FY2028 FCF does not collapse with revenue. FY2036 revenue ~6.2bn.

scenario_narratives.base: MPWR holds its position as a primary power-delivery supplier on current-generation AI accelerator and CPU platforms and wins a fair but not dominant share of the next generation, while automotive, communications/optical and storage grow at semiconductor-normal rates. Revenue rises 38% in FY2027 off the Q4-2026 run-rate and then decelerates sharply as hyperscaler capex growth normalises; the ~8bn capacity being installed for H2-2027 is filled only around FY2030. Gross margin stays ~55% because AI power modules carry lower margins than legacy discrete ICs, so operating leverage comes only from opex; SBC stays elevated through the 2026 MPSU vesting period. This is a high-quality analog compounder growing ~10%/yr for a decade from an elevated base, with owner-FCF margins maturing around 21%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The bull axes are share and content on Nvidia's Vera Rubin / Rubin Ultra platforms (supply-chain estimates of up to ~70% of certain sockets, at higher ASPs), the move to 800V DC datacenter power where MPWR is sampling high-voltage products, and AI networking pulling Communications along. AI capex keeps growing through 2028, the ~8bn of capacity is absorbed on schedule, and non-AI segments add a cyclical recovery. Revenue reaches ~8.3bn in FY2028 and ~17.5bn by FY2036 with pre-SBC margins expanding to 42%. This needs several things to go right at once: no socket loss at a generation change, no AI digestion phase, and no export-control hit to a business with ~93% of sales in Asia.
scenario_narratives.bear: The bear axis is that the fastest-growing 42% of revenue is substantially one platform relationship that already broke once: in 2024 Enterprise Data fell on order cancellations amid a voltage-regulator quality dispute now the subject of a securities class action. Each Nvidia generation and the 800V transition is a fresh bid against Infineon, TI, ADI and onsemi. In this path an AI-capex digestion and/or a lost socket halves Enterprise Data in FY2028, distributors (top three = 54% of revenue) destock, capacity installed for 8bn sits underused, and tariffs or export controls weigh on China-linked demand. Revenue falls 15% in FY2028 and recovers slowly; margins compress to the low-to-mid 30s pre-SBC. The business remains solidly profitable and net cash - this is an earnings reset, not a solvency case; the terminal value does not approach the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: the growth thesis rests on a single platform customer (Nvidia) behind the largest segment, with a 2024 precedent of cancellations, plus an unremediated material weakness and open litigation. Base 50%: continued leadership with normalising AI growth is the central reading of guidance and the capacity plan. Bull cut to 25%: it requires share gains at a generation change, an uninterrupted AI capex cycle and no trade-policy disruption simultaneously.

valuation_philosophy.summary: MPWR is valued as a durable, high-return analog franchise on the cash it leaves owners after stock compensation, working capital and capacity capex - not on the current AI-driven growth rate. FY2026's +55% is treated as a step-change in the revenue base that the model accepts in full, followed by deliberate deceleration, because the incremental revenue is concentrated in one customer platform and semiconductor demand is cyclical. Risk is charged once, through scenario paths and weights, at a single 10% discount rate. The market price implies that hypergrowth persists for several more years at expanding margins; all three scenarios sit below it, so the finding is that the stock prices in more than the bull path, not that the business is weak.
key_risks_to_valuation: Single-platform concentration: Enterprise Data (42% of revenue) depends heavily on Nvidia design wins that are re-bid each generation; a lost socket moves the outcome toward the bear path.
AI capex cyclicality: FY2027-28 growth is the largest swing factor; each 10pp of FY2027 growth moves base value by roughly 7%.
Upside risk to the model: if the ~8bn capacity is filled by 2028 rather than 2030 at 40%+ pre-SBC margins, value approaches or exceeds the bull case.
SBC: the 2026 MPSU grants (~570-600 of cost over three years) lifted SBC to ~9% of revenue; the path assumes it glides to 6.5%.
Tax: material weakness in deferred-tax controls and a restated FY2024; the 1,183 deferred tax asset is excluded from the bridge and the cash-tax rate is assumed at ~22% with no shelter.
Geopolitics: ~93% of sales to Asia; tariffs and AI export controls.
Working capital: inventory and receivables absorb ~18% of incremental revenue; faster growth costs more cash up front.
